themes._comment: Per-theme minimal-blast-radius map (Trevor, 2026-07-13). Each js/themes/*.js file resolves to its ONE level screenshot (regenerate with `capture`, not the all-levels catch-all above) and the research/wiki page that GROUNDS its signature mechanic (theme-authoring.md's wiki-fidelity rule: the scene must show the original game's real play, judged against this page, never model memory). When a theme file changes, refresh its `screenshot` and re-check the theme against its `research` page. Every theme also carries rules .claude/rules/theme-authoring.md + its act file (see levels.md). `research: null` = not a game with a wiki page (terminal/high-score/word-processor) OR a known research gap (see notes). Source of truth: docs/features/level-themes.md frontmatter; keep both in sync. Keyed by theme file; the `js/themes/` entry in `features` remains the coarse fallback.

js/themes/terminal.js.note: Command line, not a game — no wiki page. Primary feature is easter-eggs (see features[]); this entry only maps its level screenshot. BLAST-RADIUS WARNING (2026-09-11): this file also EXPORTS the Act 4 white rabbit (resetWhiteRabbit/maybeWhiteRabbit/drawWhiteRabbit), imported by simcity.js, goldeneye.js, ageofempires.js and ff7.js — so a change to the RABBIT touches levels 16-20, not just 20, while a change to the terminal scene itself (incl. the frozen Y2K clock) touches only this screenshot.

tracks._comment: Per-track minimal-blast-radius map (2026-09-13), the exact analogue of `themes` above for Act 7's racing wing. Each js/speedway/tracks/*.js file resolves to the capture SUBSET that regenerates only its own frames (never the whole speedway set) and the research/wiki page that GROUNDS its era and its signature mechanic — the same wiki-fidelity rule theme-authoring.md imposes on js/themes/*: the scene must show what the original machine actually did, judged against the research graph, never model memory. Every track also carries rules docs/specs/act7-speed-racing.md + .claude/rules/product.md. NOTE the asymmetry with `themes`: a change to js/speedway/render/kit.js or js/speedway/track.js affects EVERY track's frames (shared engine + shared render vocabulary), so those regenerate the whole set — only the files below are per-track. Source of truth: docs/features/speedway.md; keep both in sync.
